doors.name: tool_schema_digest
doors.note: Language 0.7, which only the Rust compiler reads: no TypeScript function of the compiler stands for it. It gives what schemaDigest of runtime/src/mcp-client.ts gives for a tool, byte for byte (the lock's sha256 of the canonical JSON of { name, inputSchema, outputSchema }), and crates/mandate-check/tests/connector_doors.rs holds it to vectors/tool-digest/tool-schema-digest.json, which scripts/tool-digest-vectors.mjs writes from that function. tool is the JSON text of the tool, not an object, so that a number keeps its JSON form.

doors.name: callable_connectors
doors.note: Language 0.7, which only the Rust compiler reads: no TypeScript function stands for it. The connectors a program can call, [{ id, name }] with id <module>.<connector>: those the check demands a lock entry for (E1407), by the same function (crate::lock::callable_connectors), for the program as the runtime has it at start.

doors.name: mcp_tools
doors.note: Language 0.7, which only the Rust compiler reads: no TypeScript function stands for it. The tools of the MCP servers of a language, { language, tools, modern }: tools is the tools member of the result of tools/list, unchanged, for both servers and both protocol eras, and modern is what the modern era adds beside it ({ ttlMs, cacheScope }). language is required, mandate/0.1 to mandate/0.7: those up to 0.6 give the frozen list (the tables door's TOOLS), 0.7 the frozen list and the changes spec/attention.md names (crates/mandate-check/tests/mcp_tools.rs holds the set of differences), and vectors/mcp-tools/mcp-tools-0.7.json holds the output.

doors.name: attention_facts
doors.note: Language 0.7, which only the Rust compiler reads: the attention facts of a workflow (spec/attention.md, The facts), from the typing of the check that checks it, with the input of the door check and the workflow's name; null when the program does not check. No TypeScript function stands for it, and crates/mandate-testkit/tests/attention_0_7.rs holds it to the fixtures of 0.7.
